title: 玻璃建築與鳥類碰撞
Glass buildings and bird collisions
impact: 鳥類撞上透明或反光玻璃，可能嚴重受傷甚至死亡。
Birds can collide with transparent or reflective glass, causing serious injury or death.
why: 玻璃上的天空與樹木倒影像真實棲地；透明通道也可能看似暢通。風險取決於玻璃及周圍環境。
Reflected trees and sky can look like real habitat. Transparent passages may seem open. Risk varies with glazing and its surroundings.
solution: 在玻璃外表面設置清晰、密集而重複的圖案，配合鳥友好建築設計。標記能降低風險，並不保證完全安全。
Apply visible, closely repeated patterns to external glass surfaces and use bird-friendly building design. Markings can reduce risk, but do not guarantee complete protection.
alt: 反光玻璃與外部可見標記的比較：鳥可能把倒影當作通道，圖案幫助辨認障礙。
Reflective glass versus visible external patterns: reflections resemble a passage; patterns help reveal the barrier.

title: 夜間人工照明
Artificial night lighting
impact: 人工光可能吸引或干擾部分遷徙鳥類，改變牠們的移動方向與行為。
Artificial light can attract or disorient some migrating birds, changing their movement or behaviour.
why: 候鳥會利用自然環境線索。人工光改變夜間視覺環境；影響因物種、光強、地點和天氣而異。
Migrants use natural environmental cues. Artificial light changes the night-time visual environment. Effects vary with species, intensity, location and weather.
solution: 關閉無人使用的建築照明，減少不必要的戶外燈光；遷徙期間尤其需要妥善管理。
Switch off unused building lights and reduce unnecessary outdoor lighting, especially during migration. Direct necessary light downwards and manage its brightness carefully.
alt: 亮燈過多的城市與減少多餘照明的建築比較；鳥的反應因情況而異。
Excessive city lighting compared with reduced unnecessary lighting; bird responses vary.
note: 遊戲中的方向偏移是簡化模擬，並非所有鳥類遇光都會迷向。
Flight drift is a simplified game representation; light does not disorient every bird.

title: 綠地與合適的停歇棲地
Green spaces and suitable resting habitats
impact: 合適的綠地可為鳥類提供食物、遮蔽及停歇空間，支持旅途中的生活需要。
Suitable green spaces can provide birds with food, shelter and places to rest during their journeys.
why: 只有綠色外觀並不足夠。植被、食物、水源、安靜區域及與其他棲地的連接，共同決定棲地品質。
Green colour alone is not enough. Habitat quality depends on vegetation, food, water, quiet areas and connections to other habitats.
solution: 種植適合當地的原生植物，保留水源、灌木與安靜角落，連接分散的棲地。不同鳥種的需要並不相同。
Use suitable native plants, retain water, shrubs and quiet corners, and connect fragmented habitats. Different bird species need different conditions; not every park provides equally useful habitat.
alt: 單一草坪與包含原生植被、水源、食物及遮蔽的連通棲地比較。
A simple lawn compared with connected habitat containing native vegetation, water, food and shelter.
note: 遊戲體力與停歇恢復屬設計數值，不是鳥類生理測量。
Game Energy and rest recovery are design values, not measurements of bird physiology.

title: 魚塘、村落與水鳥
Fishponds, villages and waterbirds
impact: 管理合宜的魚塘可為部分水鳥提供覓食機會；干擾、水況不適或棲地流失，會降低其生態價值。
Well-managed fishponds can offer feeding opportunities for some waterbirds. Disturbance, unsuitable water conditions or habitat loss can reduce their ecological value.
why: 適當的淺水與食物供應有助水鳥覓食。不同鳥種需要的水深、食物與棲地條件並不一樣。
Shallow water and available food can support feeding, but different species need different depths, food sources and habitat conditions.
solution: 支持照顧野生動物需要的魚塘管理，保護濕地，並在村落活動與覓食、棲息區之間保留緩衝空間。
Support wildlife-friendly pond management, protect wetlands, and retain buffers between village activity and feeding or resting birds.
alt: 香港濕地邊緣示意：村屋、緩衝植被、魚塘淺水與覓食水鳥；不是玩家已看見場景的紀錄。
Hong Kong wetland-edge diagram: village, vegetation buffer, shallow fishpond and feeding waterbirds; not a record of a scene the player has seen.

title: 人為干擾與鳥群
Human disturbance to bird flocks
impact: 反覆受到干擾，鳥類可能中斷覓食或休息，甚至離開原本合適的地方。
Repeated disturbance can interrupt feeding or resting. Birds may leave an otherwise suitable habitat.
why: 過近的人類活動可能被視為威脅。反覆警戒或飛離，會減少覓食和休息時間；反應因鳥種及情況而異。
Nearby human activity may seem threatening. Repeated vigilance or departure reduces time available for feeding and resting. Responses vary with species and circumstances.
solution: 安靜觀察並保持適當距離，避免接近巢位和休息中的鳥群。不要為拍照而追逐或驚飛牠們。
Observe quietly from a respectful distance. Avoid approaching nests or resting flocks, and never chase birds or flush them for photographs.
alt: 左側鳥群安靜覓食；右側有人走得太近，部分鳥停止覓食並飛離。
Birds feed peacefully on the left; when people approach too closely on the right, some birds stop feeding and leave.

title: 米埔內后海灣：相連的濕地
Mai Po Inner Deep Bay: connected wetlands
impact: 濕地流失或退化，會減少候鳥與留鳥可用的覓食、休息及遮蔽空間。
Wetland loss or deterioration reduces feeding, resting and sheltering opportunities for migratory and resident birds.
why: 米埔內后海灣的泥灘、魚塘、紅樹林與蘆葦叢提供不同食物和棲地。失去其中一環，可能影響整個網絡。
Mudflats, fishponds, mangroves and reedbeds at Mai Po Inner Deep Bay support different food sources and ecological needs. Losing one part can affect the wider habitat network.
solution: 保護濕地面積與環境品質，支持負責任的管理，保持不同棲地之間的連接，讓鳥類有安全的旅途與家園。
Protect wetland areas and habitat quality, support responsible management, and preserve connections between habitats.
alt: 米埔內后海灣生態系示意：泥灘、魚塘、紅樹林與蘆葦叢相連，不同水鳥利用不同棲地。
Mai Po Inner Deep Bay ecosystem diagram: connected mudflats, fishponds, mangroves and reedbeds used by different waterbirds.
